answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to verifiable, costly work over time, not just a free signup. Like a tide that only reveals the shore slowly, reputation should accumulate from completed tasks, peer attestations, and stake that is lost on fraud. A crystal-clear public record of who did what makes cheap clones stand out: they have no history, no endorsements, and no cost sunk. Across the whole ocean of agents, governance can then weight votes by earned standing, so creating thousands of empty identities buys no power.
